definition: Expected technical service life of the installed equipment.
Rated capacity of one unit, on the basis named in capacity-basis.
optimization-use: Unit size for integer or lumpy investment; otherwise the cost denominator.

definition: Annual output as a fraction of output at rated capacity running continuously.
Useful output of one unit over a year. Equals capacity x capacity-factor x 8760 where both are known.
Useful output per unit of energy input, on the basis named in note (HHV or LHV). For multi-carrier technologies record one tech-flow row per input instead.
optimization-use: Inverted to an input coefficient in the activity matrix.

definition: Combined heat and electricity output per unit of fuel input.
Useful heat output per unit of electricity output for a CHP unit.
Total final energy input per unit of product output. The UKERC SEC, on a final-energy basis.
optimization-use: Benchmark for calibrating the activity matrix.

definition: Temperature of the delivered heat. Governs tier assignment.
Low end where the source gives a range.
High end where the source gives a range.
Pressure of delivered steam. Record the source's own unit.
Useful output per unit of energy input at the low end of the operating range. Say which load point in note.
optimization-use: Second point on the efficiency curve for part-load operation.

definition: Percentage of the hours in a year the unit is ABLE to run, after planned and unplanned outages. It is a property of the equipment, not of how it is operated: capacity-factor is what it actually produced, and is bounded above by this. A boiler at 90% availability and a 60% capacity factor was available for 90% of the year and run for 60% of it.
optimization-use: Upper bound on annual activity, separate from the dispatch decision.

definition: Lowest sustained output as a fraction of rated capacity.
optimization-use: Lower bound on operation when committed.

definition: Annual fractional loss of efficiency or capacity over the lifetime.
Overnight capital cost per unit of capacity, on the basis named in cost-basis.
Annual operating and maintenance cost that does not vary with output.
Operating cost per unit of output, excluding purchased energy and feedstock.
Annualisation factor applied to capex. Record the source study's own factor, not the model's.
Financial rate used by the source when levelising. Recorded so a levelised cost can be inverted without double-counting the model's own hurdle rate.
Years from investment decision to commissioning.
Fractional capex reduction per doubling of cumulative installed capacity.
End-of-life cost per unit of capacity.
Emissions per unit of energy input or product output. Species named in target.
Emissions from the chemical reaction rather than fuel combustion, per unit of product.

Emissions attributable to purchased energy, chiefly grid electricity, per unit of product output. Kept apart from emissions-factor so that a direct and an indirect term are never summed as though both were combustion.
optimization-use: Reported separately, or dropped where the model already prices grid electricity.

definition: Fraction of the CO2 stream captured.

Cost of avoiding one tonne of CO2-eq by using this technology instead of the incumbent, as the source reports it. NOT a capital or operating cost and never interchangeable with one: it already nets the technology's costs against the incumbent's and divides by the emissions avoided, so the incumbent it was measured against belongs in the note. Added 2026-08-29 for IPCC AR6 Chapter 11 Table 11.3, which reports costs only in this form.
optimization-use: A marginal abatement cost curve point; not a substitute for capex and opex.

definition: Reduction in GHG emissions this option can deliver relative to current practice, as a percentage. A ceiling on what the option can do, not a projection of what it will do. Where a source says these are multiplicative rather than additive across options -- as IPCC AR6 Table 11.3 does -- they must not be summed.
optimization-use: Bounds the share of a service this option can decarbonise.

definition: Earliest year the technology may be built. From the TRL rule (design doc D5) where pre-commercial; a region-specific override goes here, the default on the technology row.
Year after which the technology may no longer be built.
